name: Stone tools
desc: Knapped flint and ground stone. Every job goes faster. The Stone Age begins.

name: Farming
desc: Planted fields. Villages can grow past the size foraging allows.

name: Granaries
desc: Stored grain survives a bad year.

name: Log raft
desc: Logs bound with kelp rope. Crosses shallow reefs.

name: Dugout canoe
desc: A hollowed log. Crosses open channels in fair weather.

name: Outrigger
desc: A float lashed to the hull. Stable in rough water.

name: Woven sail
desc: Leaf-mat sails. Trips of several days.

name: Star navigation
desc: Star counts and bird lore. Crossings beyond sight of land, and back.

name: Colony fleet
desc: Several boats sail together to settle a new shore.

name: Herb lore
desc: Doctors know which leaves break a fever.

name: Quarantine custom
desc: The sick are kept apart. Plague spreads far less.

name: Bow and obsidian
desc: Weapons that kill at a distance.

name: Palisade
desc: A wall of sharpened logs around the village.

name: Shield wall
desc: Woven shields and long spears. Trained war bands.

name: War canoe
desc: Raids across the sea.

name: Stone fort
desc: Stone walls and a sea gate.

name: Weaving
desc: Rope, cloth and mats. Sails become possible.

name: Pottery
desc: Pots store grain and water.

name: Salting
desc: Salted fish and meat keep through winter and long voyages.

name: Masonry
desc: Fitted stone. Stone houses and walls.

name: Brickmaking
desc: Clay fired in kilns. Brick houses and granaries.

name: Copperworking
desc: The first metal, hammered into blades and ornaments.

name: Bronze
desc: Copper and tin smelted together. The Bronze Age begins.

name: Writing
desc: Marks on clay. Laws, records and the first histories.

name: The wheel
desc: The potter's wheel turned on its side. Carts carry stone and grain along the tracks.

name: Paved roads
desc: Stone-laid streets and roads between towns. Stores and builders move faster.

name: Town planning
desc: Streets laid out in a grid, with a market square, a palace and a harbour. Cities become possible.

name: Iron
desc: Ore smelted in hot furnaces. Cheap, hard tools and blades for everyone. The Classical age begins.

name: Coinage
desc: Stamped metal. Trade flows faster and tribute is easier to count.

name: Written law
desc: Laws cut in stone. Rulers seem fairer and the people grumble less.

name: Aqueducts
desc: Clean water carried on arches into the cities. Fewer die of sickness.

name: Philosophy
desc: Schools where people argue about everything. New ideas come faster.

name: Siegecraft
desc: Rams and catapults. Walls protect less against an army that has them.

name: Lighthouses
desc: Fires on stone towers guide ships home. Fewer are lost.

name: War galleys
desc: Oared warships with rams. Raids across the sea hit harder.

name: The compass
desc: A needle that always points north, even under cloud.

name: Printing
desc: Books by the hundred. Knowledge spreads to everyone who can read.

name: Gunpowder
desc: Saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur. Cannon on walls and ships.

name: Ocean ships
desc: Deep-hulled ships with square sails that can cross the open ocean. The Age of Sail begins, and the world grows.

name: Cartography
desc: Printed charts. A tribe learns every coast its friends have seen.

name: The steam engine
desc: Coal boils water and the steam drives pistons. Mines are pumped dry and the Industrial age begins.

name: Steel
desc: Iron refined in roaring furnaces. Stronger tools, rails and hulls.

name: Factories
desc: Engines drive looms and lathes. Towns make far more, and burn far more coal.

name: Railways
desc: Iron roads and locomotives join the towns of an island.

name: Steamships
desc: Steel hulls, screws and funnels. They cross the ocean on schedule, whatever the wind.

name: Vaccines
desc: A little of the sickness, to teach the body to fight it. Plagues kill a fraction of what they did.

name: Rifles
desc: Rifled barrels and cartridges. Armies hit harder, from further away.

name: The telegraph
desc: Messages along copper wires, faster than any horse or ship. Ideas spread quickly.

name: Fertilizer
desc: Factory-made fertilizer. Harvests rise, and so do the towns.
